constitution.title: Katiba ya Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania ya Mwaka 1977
constitution.note: Constitution of the United Republic as posted by INEC under election laws. Arts. 38-42 (President, elected by the most votes, Art. 41(6); five-year term, Art. 42(2)), 65 (five-year life of Parliament), 66 (classes of member of Parliament), 74 (Electoral Commission), 75 (constituencies), 78 (women's special seats), and 109 and 118 (judges appointed by the President).

zanzibar_constitution.title: Katiba ya Zanzibar ya 1984 (Toleo la 2010)

election_act_2024.title: Sheria ya Uchaguzi wa Rais, Wabunge na Madiwani ya Mwaka 2024

inec_act_2024.title: Sheria ya Tume Huru ya Taifa ya Uchaguzi ya Mwaka 2024
inec_act_2024.note: Act No. 2 of 2024. S. 10(1): INEC runs the President, Parliament, and Mainland councillor elections, the village, mtaa, and kitongoji elections under a law Parliament is to enact, and names the women's special seats.

laea_2015.title: The Local Authorities (Elections) Act, Cap. 292 (Revised Edition 2015)

classes.name: Chaguzi ndogo (Zanzibar)
classes.name_en: By-elections to the Zanzibar House of Representatives and Zanzibar ward councils
classes.locator: https://www.zec.go.tz/admin_panel/public/Sheria-uchaguzi/1779948493_ELECTION%20ACT%204%20OF%202018_compressed.pdf (by-elections for vacant seats; ZEC's election cycle lists "Chaguzi Ndogo" after the general election)
classes.note: ZEC lists by-elections in its post-election cycle; no by-election return was found among its publications.

classes.name: Kura ya Maoni (Zanzibar)
classes.name_en: Zanzibar referendums under the Referendum Act, 2010
classes.locator: https://www.inec.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1714455504-1.%20sw-1675241093-sw1489729212-Katiba_ya_Zanzibar_ya_1984_(Toleo_la_2010)_sw.pdf (s. 80A: amendments to listed sections need approval "na wananchi kwa Kura ya Maoni", added by Act No. 9 of 2010)
classes.note: ZEC ran one referendum, in July 2010, on the government of national unity that the tenth amendment (Act No. 9 of 2010) then wrote into the Constitution. The Referendum Act and the 2010 report are page images, and the polling day was not confirmed in a source read here.

dates.note: Referendum on the government of national unity; ZEC's Referendum Act No. 6 of 2010 governed it. The day is not in a text source reached here.

classes.name: Kura ya Maoni ya Katiba Inayopendekezwa
classes.name_en: Union constitutional referendum on the Proposed Constitution
classes.note: The Union Constitution (Art. 98) is amended by a two-thirds majority of Parliament with no referendum. The Constitutional Review Act and the Referendum Act, 2013 provided a single referendum on the Proposed Constitution of 2014, which was postponed in 2015 and never held.
classes.disposition_reason: No Union-wide referendum has ever been held; the 2015 vote on the Proposed Constitution was postponed and never rescheduled. The class stays so one would be classified if held.

classes.name: Baraza la Kutunga Sheria (Majilis Tashrii) 1957-1963
classes.name_en: Zanzibar Protectorate Legislative Council and National Assembly elections
classes.locator: https://www.zec.go.tz/admin_panel/public/taarifa-uchaguzi/1752063954_RIPOTI%20YA%20UCHAGUZI%20MKUU%20ZANZIBAR%202020.._compressed.pdf (s. 1.4.1: "Uchaguzi wa mwanzo wa Zanzibar ulifanyika mwaka 1957")
classes.note: Six elected seats in 1957, 22 in January 1961, 23 in June 1961, and 31 in July 1963, under an election commissioner appointed by the British Resident. Ended by the revolution of 12 January 1964; no election followed until 1980.

classes.name: Baraza la Kutunga Sheria (LegCo) na Bunge la Tanganyika 1958-1960
classes.name_en: Tanganyika Legislative Council and National Assembly elections before the Union
classes.locator: https://www.parliament.go.tz/pages/history ("Katika Uchaguzi Mkuu uliofanyika Februari, 1958, Baraza lilipata Wajumbe wa kuchaguliwa")
classes.note: The first elected members joined the Council at the election Parliament's history dates to February 1958, then the 1960 election that made every seat elective and renamed the body the National Assembly. Tanganyika's direct presidential election of 1962 is class tanganyika_president.

dates.quote: Katika Uchaguzi Mkuu uliofanyika Februari, 1958, Baraza lilipata Wajumbe wa kuchaguliwa

classes.name: Uchaguzi wa Rais wa Jamhuri ya Tanganyika (1962)
classes.name_en: President of the Republic of Tanganyika, 1962
classes.note: Tanganyika became a republic on 9 December 1962 after a direct presidential election earlier that year; no official source reached here records the poll or its date, so the class has no dated row.

classes.name: Viti Maalum vya Wanawake (Bunge, Baraza la Wawakilishi na Halmashauri)
classes.name_en: Women's special seats in Parliament, the House of Representatives, and councils
classes.locator: https://www.inec.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1714455356-1.%20sw-1675190712-sw1499671152-Katiba_ya_Tanzania.pdf (Art. 66(1)(b) and 78: seats allocated to parties in proportion to their share)
classes.disposition_reason: No vote is cast for these seats: INEC and ZEC allocate them from each party's share of the constituency vote or seats and gazette the nominees (INEC Gazette of 4 December 2020).

classes.name: Chaguzi zisizo za moja kwa moja
classes.name_en: Indirect elections: Bunge members chosen by the House of Representatives, East African Legislative Assembly members, and speakers
classes.locator: https://www.inec.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1714455356-1.%20sw-1675190712-sw1499671152-Katiba_ya_Tanzania.pdf (Art. 66(1)(c): "Wabunge watano waliochaguliwa na Baraza la Wawakilishi kutoka miongoni mwa wajumbe wake")
classes.disposition_reason: Members of a chamber choose these office holders among themselves; no voter casts a ballot and no public returns are published. Until 1990 Parliament also elected 15 national members and 15 women from party lists (INEC 1985 report).

classes.name: Kura za maoni za vyama
classes.locator: https://www.inec.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1714458586-SHERIA%20YA%20UCHAGUZI%20WA%20RAIS,%20WABUNGE%20NA%20MADIWANI%20YA%20MWAKA%202024.pdf (candidates must be nominated by a registered party)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties run their own nominations; the state does not run or publish them.

classes.name: Majaji
classes.locator: https://www.inec.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1714455356-1.%20sw-1675190712-sw1499671152-Katiba_ya_Tanzania.pdf (Arts. 109 and 118: the President appoints the judges of the High Court and the Court of Appeal)
classes.disposition_reason: Tanzania elects no judges; all are appointed.
